newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostage negotiations seen under way.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage negotiations seen under way.

text.p: Face-to-face talks on the Lima hostage drama between Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) spokesman Rolly Rojas apparently started on Tuesday afternoon.

"We assume Rojas has gone in and the talks have started. That was the plan, and from what I saw, everything went according to that plan," Red Cross spokeswoman Cecile Baux told Reuters after a Red Cross car, apparently with Rojas inside, went from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence to a nearby house selected for negotiations.
Rojas, known by his nom de guerre "The Arab", is the second-in-command of the MRTA unit holding 72 hostages inside the residence in the San Isidro neighbourhood of Lima.
The 34-year-old former busfare collector was selected by the MRTA to represent them in the first round of formal talks.
President Alberto Fujimori said MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini would probably take part in later "definitive" talks to resolve the 56-day-old crisis.
MRTA rebels have been holding the residence, where they initially took more than 500 captives, since they stormed a lavish cocktail party there on Dec. 17.
